task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output:
User: Hello... yes, hi. I'm having trouble with my phone. The internet on it — the mobile data — it either doesn't work at all or it's just so terribly slow. I can't get anything to load. I was hoping you could help me fix it?

I should mention, I'm John Smith, and my number is 555-123-2002. And... I'm in France right now, visiting. I don't have any Wi-Fi here, so it's just the phone data.

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get your data working while you're in France. Let me start by pulling up your account.

I've found your account and the line you're using (555-123-2002). I can see that your line is active and roaming is enabled for international use, but there's one main issue causing your data problems: your line has used 15.1 GB out of the 15.0 GB data limit on your Premium Plan, so you've gone over your monthly data allowance.

Your billing cycle resets on 2025-02-28, but since you need data now in France, you have two options:

1. **Refuel data** — add up to 2 GB to your line at $2.00 per GB (your plan's refueling rate).
2. **Change to a plan with more data.**

Could you let me know which option you'd prefer? If you'd like to refuel, just tell me how much data you'd like to add (up to 2 GB) and I'll confirm the price before applying it.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh dear... I've gone over? I didn't even realize. That's a bit worrying to hear, I must say.

Well, I definitely don't want to change my plan — that sounds complicated and I don't want to mess anything up. So... the refueling one, please. Let's do the 2 GB, the full amount, since I'd like this to actually work properly. That's $4.00, is that right?

And once that's done, will my internet be fast again? I really need it to be good — not just a little better, but properly fast.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Done — I've added 2 GB of data to your line 555-123-2002 for $4.00, which will appear on your bill.

Regarding speed: the refuel restores your data **connection**, but it doesn't change the underlying speed of the network you're connected to. Since you're roaming in France, your speed depends on the local network available to you there, and roaming connections can sometimes be slower than at home. I can't guarantee a particular speed.

To give your connection the best chance of being as fast as possible, could you check a couple of things on your phone for me?

1. Please run a **speed test** (to see what speed you're actually getting right now).
2. Please check your **status bar** and tell me what it shows (signal strength, network type such as 5G/4G, and whether data is enabled).
3. Please check that **Data Saver** is turned off, and that **Data Roaming** is turned on in your phone's settings.

Once you tell me what those show, I can guide you through the next steps if anything needs adjusting.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try to do those things... I'll see what I can find. One moment.

turns.thought:
Good news — nothing is broken, and you certainly didn't damage anything. Airplane Mode simply switches off all of your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth) at once. With it ON, there's no signal at all, which is exactly why the speed test reported "No Connection." It's a very common thing to switch on by accident — often by a button in the quick settings panel when the phone is in a pocket or bag.

Let's fix this one step at a time, starting with the main cause. Please do this:

**Step 1:** Turn Airplane Mode **OFF**. On most phones you swipe down from the top of the screen to open the quick settings panel, then tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted. Some phones instead have it under Settings → Network & internet (or Connections) → Airplane mode.

Once you've done that, please check your status bar again and tell me what it shows — particularly whether you now see signal bars and a network type (like 4G or 5G). I'll then walk you through the remaining items (mobile data, data roaming and Data Saver).
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, thank goodness. That's a relief to hear — I was quite worried for a moment there.

Alright, let me try to turn that airplane thing off. One moment...

turns.thought:
That's great news — "Excellent" signal with 5G means your phone has reconnected to the cellular network beautifully. You're right that "Data Disabled" isn't right, though; that just means the mobile data switch is still turned off, so your phone has service but isn't allowed to use it for internet. That's the next thing to fix.

**Step 2:** Please turn Mobile Data **ON**. On most phones:
- Swipe down from the top of the screen to open quick settings, and tap the **Mobile data** (or "Cellular data") tile so it lights up / shows as on.
- Or go to Settings → Network & internet (or Connections) → **Mobile network** and switch **Mobile data** on.

Once that's done, please check your status bar again and tell me what it shows. After that we'll handle Data Roaming and Data Saver — both of which matter for using data here in France.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning the mobile data on now...

turns.thought:
You're doing really well. Yes — that's exactly the one. Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make apps slow or unresponsive and slow your connection down. Since you want your internet working properly in France, let's switch it off.

**Step 3:** Turn **Data Saver OFF**:
- Swipe down from the top of the screen to open quick settings and look for the **Data Saver** tile (often shown with a downward arrow icon) — tap it so it's no longer highlighted.
- Or go to Settings → Network & internet (or Connections) → **Data Saver** (sometimes called "Data Saver mode"), and switch it **Off**.

You won't break anything by turning it off — it's just a data-saving feature, and it can be switched back on any time.

Once that's done, please check your data restriction status or status bar and confirm Data Saver is off. We still have one more item after this: **Data Roaming** on your phone, which is important while you're in France.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll turn that Data Saver off then. Here goes...

turns.thought:
Good question — and yes, this one matters while you're abroad. Data Roaming is the phone-level switch that lets your phone use a foreign network's data (your line here in France). With it off, your phone won't use mobile data outside our home network, even with data enabled.

The good news on cost: your **line is already roaming-enabled**, and enabling roaming on the line is done at no cost — that part is already in place, so there's no extra charge for turning this on.

**Step 4:** Turn **Data Roaming ON** on your phone:
- Swipe down from the top of the screen to open quick settings, long-press (or tap the gear under) the **Mobile data / Cellular data** tile, and look for **Roaming** (sometimes under "Network & internet" → "Mobile network" → "Roaming").
- Switch **Data roaming** (sometimes called "Roaming data") to **On**.

A couple of reassuring notes so you don't worry:
- The 2 GB you purchased is the data allowance for your line this cycle, and it applies to the data you use. I can't provide a detailed breakdown of any roaming usage charges beyond the refuel rate we already applied ($2.00/GB), so if you'd like full detail on international roaming charges, I can transfer you to a human agent who can go through that with you.

Please go ahead and turn Data Roaming on, and then run the **speed test** again and tell me what it reports. Once it shows a speed, I'll help interpret it — and if it's still slow or showing no connection, we'll keep working through it together.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll turn the roaming on. I do appreciate you explaining the cost bit — I was a bit nervous about that.
